theme: The 48-Hour Pre-Event Briefing That Prevents 80% of On-Site Surprises

linkedin.text:
After producing 1,500+ corporate events across 130+ destinations, here's the single operational habit that separates smooth executions from expensive fire drills:

A mandatory 48-hour pre-event briefing — structured, not social.

Not a recap of the run-of-show. A live alignment session where every decision owner is named out loud: who approves a last-minute room flip, who calls the AV team if the keynote mic drops, who has the venue manager's direct line.

When you can answer those questions before the day starts, you stop managing people on-site and start managing the experience.

The events that run cleanly aren't the ones with the biggest budgets. They're the ones where accountability was assigned before anything could go wrong.

CMOs and HR leaders — what pre-event discipline has saved you most often? I'm genuinely curious what the field has figured out.

instagram.text:
Most event fires? They start 48 hours before, not on the day.

After 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations, the pattern is clear: chaos on-site almost always traces back to a gap in the pre-event briefing.

One structured session. Every vendor. Every stakeholder. Every decision owner — named.

That's how 600-person conferences run on schedule. 💡

facebook.text:
One thing we've learned across 1,500+ events: most on-site chaos is preventable.

The fix? A structured 48-hour pre-event briefing — not a call to check boxes, but a session where every vendor, venue rep, and internal stakeholder walks out knowing exactly who owns every decision.

When everyone knows their lane, day-of problems shrink dramatically. When they don't, you spend your event managing people instead of the experience.

Small operational discipline. Massive difference in outcome.

What's the one pre-event step your team never skips? Drop it in the comments — we're always collecting field-tested ideas.
